questions.prompt: Why do you want to work as a software engineer at this company?
questions.sampleAnswer:
Connect your experience to the company’s products, users, and engineering challenges—cite a specific product behaviour or tech blog insight. Explain how the role’s scope (product eng, platform, etc.) matches skills you want to deepen.

Close with mutual fit: what you deliver in the first 6–12 months and what you hope to learn. Avoid generic “great culture” without evidence.

questions.prompt: Walk me through your résumé, focusing on impact.
questions.sampleAnswer:
Narrate 2–3 roles/projects with the formula: problem → your actions → measurable result (latency, revenue, reliability, users). Keep each to ~1 minute.

Invite deeper dives. Interviewers use this to choose follow-up technical threads.

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a teammate or manager about a technical decision.
questions.sampleAnswer:
STAR: disagreement topic, how you sought to understand their constraints, data or prototype you brought, how you committed after a decision, and outcome.

Emphasize “disagree and commit” professionalism and user impact.

questions.prompt: Describe a time you dealt with ambiguity on a project.
questions.sampleAnswer:
Explain how you clarified success metrics, listed unknowns, ran a time-boxed spike, and delivered an incremental milestone. Quantify reduced uncertainty.

Ambiguity handling is a frequent FAANG-style behavioural theme.

questions.prompt: Tell me about a production incident you helped resolve.
questions.sampleAnswer:
STAR: detection, mitigation to restore service, root-cause analysis, permanent fix, and follow-up (runbook, tests, dashboards). Stress communication during the incident.

Show calm ownership rather than blame.

questions.prompt: Give an example of receiving critical code review feedback and how you responded.
questions.sampleAnswer:
Describe the feedback, what was valid, changes you made, and how it improved later reviews. If you disagreed, explain how you discussed trade-offs respectfully.

Growth mindset is the signal.

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you mentored someone or raised the engineering bar.
questions.sampleAnswer:
Actions might include pairing, design docs, improving CI, or documenting onboarding. Result: mentee independence or fewer repeated bugs.

Leadership without title matters at mid levels.

questions.prompt: Describe a deadline trade-off: how did you protect quality while shipping?
questions.sampleAnswer:
Explain options considered (cut scope, feature flags, defer non-critical polish), risk assessment, stakeholder alignment, and post-ship follow-up.

Show product sense + engineering integrity.

questions.prompt: How do you approach a new coding interview problem on the whiteboard or editor?
questions.sampleAnswer:
Restate requirements, ask about constraints and edge cases, work an example, propose brute force, analyze complexity, then optimize. Narrate trade-offs and test the final approach.

This meta-answer is itself frequently evaluated.

questions.prompt: Implement or outline how to find whether two strings are anagrams. Discuss complexity.
questions.sampleAnswer:
Sort both O(n log n) or count characters O(n) with fixed alphabet. Discuss Unicode caveats and early exit on length mismatch.

Clean communication + complexity is the bar.

questions.prompt: Explain BFS vs DFS. When is each preferable?
questions.sampleAnswer:
BFS explores by layers—good for shortest paths in unweighted graphs. DFS explores deep paths—good for cycle detection, topological patterns, path existence.

Discuss recursion stack limits vs explicit stacks/queues and graph representations.

questions.prompt: How would you detect duplicates in a large stream of IDs with limited memory?
questions.sampleAnswer:
Discuss hash sets when memory allows; otherwise Bloom filters (probabilistic), external sort + scan, or partitioning by hash to disk.

Show ability to adapt algorithms to constraints—SWE interview staple.

questions.prompt: Compare arrays, linked lists, and dynamic arrays (vectors). Practical trade-offs?
questions.sampleAnswer:
Arrays: contiguous, O(1) index, costly insert mid. Linked lists: O(1) insert given pointer, poor cache locality. Dynamic arrays: amortized append, occasional resize.

Relate to real language structures (ArrayList, slice).

questions.prompt: When would you use a heap / priority queue?
questions.sampleAnswer:
Use for repeated retrieval of min/max: Dijkstra, scheduling, streaming top-k. Describe sift operations at high level and O(log n) updates.

Give a production-flavoured example (job scheduler).

questions.prompt: Explain hash tables: collision strategies and load factor.
questions.sampleAnswer:
Cover chaining vs open addressing, load factor impact on performance, and need for good hash functions. Mention resizing costs.

Discuss when keys are adversarial and you need stronger hashing.

questions.prompt: Design a URL shortener. What components and failure modes do you consider?
questions.sampleAnswer:
Requirements, API, ID generation, storage, cache, redirects, analytics. Discuss uniqueness, hot keys, and monitoring. Scale reads with caching/CDN.

Classic SWE system design prompt.

questions.prompt: How would you design a rate limiter for an API?
questions.sampleAnswer:
Clarify limits (per user/IP), algorithms (token bucket, sliding window), storage (Redis), and response behaviour (429 + headers). Discuss distributed coordination and bypass for internal traffic.

Tie to fairness and abuse prevention.

questions.prompt: Explain horizontal vs vertical scaling and when you choose each.
questions.sampleAnswer:
Vertical: bigger machine—simpler but capped. Horizontal: more nodes—needs statelessness, sharding, load balancing. Discuss cost, failure domains, and operational complexity.

Give an example from a service you know.

questions.prompt: What is idempotency, and why does it matter for APIs?
questions.sampleAnswer:
Idempotent operations can be retried safely without duplicating side effects. Payment charges need idempotency keys so timeouts do not double-bill.

Explain server-side storage of request keys and responses.

questions.prompt: How do you write a good design document?
questions.sampleAnswer:
Context, goals/non-goals, proposals considered, detailed design, data model/API, risks, rollout/monitoring, and open questions. Keep it reviewable and decision-oriented.

Share a time a design doc prevented rework.

questions.prompt: What makes a pull request easy to review?
questions.sampleAnswer:
Small focused diffs, clear description, test plan, screenshots for UI, and self-review first. Avoid drive-by refactors mixed with features.

Mentions CI green and risk notes.

questions.prompt: How do you approach technical debt versus new features?
questions.sampleAnswer:
Frame debt as risk/interest: prioritize by user impact and developer velocity. Propose budgeting capacity, measuring pain (build times, Sev frequency), and incremental paydown.

Speak to stakeholder communication.

questions.prompt: How do you decide what to unit test vs integration test vs e2e test?
questions.sampleAnswer:
Pyramid: many fast unit tests for logic; fewer integration tests for DB/API contracts; sparse e2e for critical user journeys. Discuss flakiness and cost.

Example from a past service.

questions.prompt: Describe your debugging process for an intermittent bug.
questions.sampleAnswer:
Reproduce reliably, gather logs/metrics/traces, form hypotheses, bisect changes, add instrumentation, fix, and add regression tests. Mention race conditions and environment parity.

Show scientific method.

questions.prompt: What are edge cases you always consider in coding problems?
questions.sampleAnswer:
Empty inputs, nulls, duplicates, overflow, negative numbers, Unicode, concurrency, and maximum constraints. State how you document assumptions.

Interviewers watch for proactive edge-case coverage.

questions.prompt: How do you communicate project status to non-engineering stakeholders?
questions.sampleAnswer:
Use outcomes and risks, not jargon: milestone progress, blockers, decisions needed, and options with trade-offs. Visuals/timelines help.

Give a STAR example of aligning a delayed launch.

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you influenced a technical decision without authority.
questions.sampleAnswer:
Describe building shared understanding via prototypes, RFCs, or customer evidence. Result: adopted approach and relationship trust.

Influence is a mid/senior SWE signal.

questions.prompt: Outline how you would merge k sorted lists efficiently.
questions.sampleAnswer:
Use a min-heap of size k for O(n log k). Contrast with pairwise merging. Discuss memory and streaming variants.

Classic heap + lists crossover question.

questions.prompt: How does a binary search tree differ from a balanced BST (e.g., AVL/red-black) in practice?
questions.sampleAnswer:
Unbalanced BSTs can degrade to O(n). Balanced trees guarantee O(log n) ops. Discuss when hash maps beat trees (unordered) vs when sorted order matters.

Practical performance awareness matters.

questions.prompt: Explain CAP and give a real product example of prioritizing availability vs consistency.
questions.sampleAnswer:
Under partition, choose AP (serve possibly stale reads) or CP (refuse/unavailable until consistent). Example: social feed freshness vs inventory reservation.

Clarify that partitions are real in WANs.

questions.prompt: How do you ensure observability for a new service?
questions.sampleAnswer:
Define SLIs/SLOs, structured logs, metrics (RED/USE), traces, and actionable alerts. Include dashboards before launch and load tests.

Tie alerts to user impact, not only CPU.

questions.prompt: What are you looking for in your next engineering role?
questions.sampleAnswer:
Discuss problem scope, mentorship/growth, tech stack learning, and impact. Align honestly with the posting without contradicting your résumé.

Ask a thoughtful question back.

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you made a mistake in production. What did you learn?
questions.sampleAnswer:
Own it, explain blast radius control, fix, communication, and systemic prevention (canary, better tests). Avoid self-flagellation without learning.

Integrity + engineering maturity.

questions.prompt: Explain quicksort vs mergesort trade-offs.
questions.sampleAnswer:
Quicksort: average O(n log n), in-place variants, poor worst case without care. Mergesort: stable O(n log n) guaranteed, needs extra memory.

Discuss practical library choices and adversarial inputs.

questions.prompt: How would you approach designing a news feed or timeline at high level?
questions.sampleAnswer:
Clarify ranking vs chronological, fan-out on write vs read, caching, and personalization. Discuss celebrity hot keys and eventual consistency.

Stay structured: requirements → API → storage → bottlenecks.

questions.prompt: What is flaky test hygiene, and why does it matter?
questions.sampleAnswer:
Flakes erode trust in CI. Practices: quarantine, fix root causes (time/order/dependency), deterministic seeds, and retry policies used sparingly.

Cultural bar for quality engineering.

questions.prompt: How do you onboard onto an unfamiliar codebase quickly?
questions.sampleAnswer:
Read architecture docs, run the app, trace a request path, make a small safe change, ask targeted questions, and document findings.

Show a past ramp-up timeline with impact.

questions.prompt: Explain feature flags and their risks.
questions.sampleAnswer:
Flags decouple deploy from release, enable canaries and experiments. Risks: flag debt, complex combinations, security if misconfigured.

Describe cleanup ownership.

questions.prompt: How do you find the k-th largest element in an unsorted array?
questions.sampleAnswer:
Quickselect average O(n), heap O(n log k), full sort O(n log n). Discuss worst cases and practical constants.

State which you’d pick under interview constraints.

questions.prompt: Do you have questions for us about the team’s engineering practices?
questions.sampleAnswer:
Ask about code review norms, on-call, deployment frequency, quality metrics, or how tech strategy decisions are made. Show you evaluate employers too.

Prepared questions signal seniority of approach.
